catalog_quote: 2b. Stress In ZANDE stress usually falls on the first syllable of disyllabic or trisyllabic words, combined in some dialects (and in BARAMBU) with slight lengthening. In some words in BARAMBU, however, it falls on the final syllable; see baa above. Stress never falls on Prefixes. [sec. 2a, same chapter:] 2a. Tone Tone is both lexical and grammatical. In ZANDE two main tone levels have been established ... [Colombaroli 1895: 389, 391] La langue A-Sandeh paraît manquer de règles stables tant pour ce qui est de la prononciation que de l'accent tonique. ... Accent tonique. — Dans les substantifs, l'accent tonique tombe ordinairement sur la première syllabe; cependant il y a beaucoup d'exceptions. Dans les adjectifs, l'accent tonique tombe toujours sur la dernière syllabe.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Zande is a tone language (two main levels, lexical and grammatical tone); non-contrastive word stress usually falls on the first syllable of di- and trisyllabic words, i.e. the first syllable of the stem, since prefixes (e.g. plural a-) are never stressed; in some dialects the stressed syllable is slightly lengthened.
new_statements.exceptions: 'usually'; prefixes never stressed; in the related language Barambu some words have final stress. Colombaroli 1895 (pp. 391-392), independently: nouns ordinarily initial accent 'with many exceptions', adjectives final, finite verbs on the tense marker or last radical syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement for di-/trisyllabic words; stem-initial once prefixes are excluded. Statement sits inside a tone-language description (tone language with a stress statement would be an equally valid label). Tucker's Zande data come from his own fieldwork (Tucker & Hackett 1959), so the statement is first-hand although published in a comparative handbook; text was recovered verbatim from archive.org full-text-search snippets of a controlled-lending scan, not from page scan.
new_statements.identity_note: Tucker's Zande material is Sudan Zande (Yambio/Tambura area; Tucker & Hackett 1959), i.e. Zande proper zand1248 rather than the Dio or Makaraka dialect entries; the same paragraph contrasts Barambu (closely related Zandic language, bara1361), where some words have final stress. Colombaroli 1895 describes 'A-Sandeh' from informants met through the Central African mission (dialect unspecified). Landi 2019 is based mainly on CAR/DRC Zande.

sources.note: pp. 389-392 'Prononciation et accent tonique': says accent placement seems to lack stable rules (same word stressed variably), then: 'Dans les substantifs, l'accent tonique tombe ordinairement sur la premiere syllabe; cependant il y a beaucoup d'exceptions. Dans les adjectifs, l'accent tonique tombe toujours sur la derniere syllabe.' Verbs: accent on the tense 'caracteristique' when present, else on the last syllable of the radical; infinitive on first syllable like nouns; in vowel sequences accent generally on the second vowel. sources.note: Only the Author's Note (pp. vii-viii) and a 'Conversations' excerpt are open (Rosetta Project); neither mentions stress. Boyd (quoted in Landi 2019: 7-8) notes Gore does not mark tone. Whether Gore has an accent statement is unknown; full text not open (Open Library 'no_ebook').

sources.citation: Landi, Germain. 2019. Phonologie et morphophonologie de la langue Zande. PhD thesis, Universitat zu Koln. xiv+237 pp. (KUPS 11370)
sources.note: Silent on stress placement. Ch. 4 'Les tons' explicitly restricts the prosodic study to lexical and grammatical tone ('Cette these se limitera a l'etude tonologique', p. 145) and the conclusion defers 'prosodologie' to future work. Literature review (p. 8) notes that Lagae & Vanden Plas 1921: 70-71 'ont souligne l'importance de l'accentuation et ont etabli les regles de fonctionnement, ou ils distinguent l'accent tonique de l'accent musical'. Describes Zande as a tone language (H, M, L), 10-vowel ATR system.

sources.citation: Landi, Germain (2019). Phonologie et morphophonologie de la langue Zande. PhD thesis, Universität zu Köln. xiv+237 pp.
sources.quote: Par contre les auteurs de ce dictionnaire ont souligné l'importance de l'accentuation et ont établi les règles de fonctionnement, où ils distinguent l'accent tonique de l'accent musical manifestent dans la phrase (Lagae et Plas 1921 : 70-71).
sources.note: Restricts prosody to tone: 'Cette thèse se limitera à l'étude tonologique, restreinte à l'étude des tons lexicaux et des tons grammaticaux' (p. 145); Zande has three tone levels (low, mid, high). No word-stress statement. Reports secondhand (p. 8) that Lagae & Vanden Plas 1921: 70-71 'ont souligné l'importance de l'accentuation et ont établi les règles de fonctionnement, où ils distinguent l'accent tonique de l'accent musical'. Also (p. 76) 'expressivité' = accenting a syllable for emphasis, realised by glottal stop or [h].
